paper_metadata.title: QLSTM4FM: Quantum Assisted Long Short-Term Memory Framework for Financial Market Trend Forecasting

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid QLSTM model with a 4‑qubit variational quantum layer (one layer with three rotation gates) for MRK stock forecasting using 2,738 trading days of Yahoo Finance data. The model reportedly uses 293 parameters versus 3,217 for a classical LSTM and shows qualitatively faster loss convergence over 20 training epochs on a PennyLane lightning.qubit simulator, but no quantitative accuracy metrics or hardware experiments are provided.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical QLSTM for daily closing-price forecasting of Merck & Co. (MRK), compared against a classical LSTM baseline using the same stock dataset and features.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) with variational quantum layers
algorithm.ansatz: one quantum layer with 3 rotational gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical data converted to quantum format via amplitude encoding; 4-qubit register used for the quantum layer
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary classification / next-day stock trend forecasting and closing-price prediction for MRK

problem_instance.description: Forecasting MRK stock trend/closing price using historical prices, technical indicators, correlated assets, and sentiment features
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance MRK dataset plus correlated assets and FinBERT sentiment features

dataset_specification.date_range: 2010-2020 (MRK visualized over this period); 2,738 trading days total
dataset_specification.preprocessing: historical prices, technical indicators, Fourier trend approximation, correlated assets, sentiment analysis

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Loaded historical stock data with yfinance/manual download; used open/close/high/low prices; computed 7-day and 21-day moving averages, 12-day and 26-day EMAs, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and momentum; applied FFT trend approximation retaining 3, 6, and 9 frequency components; added correlated assets; applied FinBERT sentiment analysis on MRK news headlines; normalized variables; used PyTorch DataLoader
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: comparison of training and test loss, prediction accuracy, convergence speed, and parameter count against classical LSTM; trained for 20 epochs

implementation_details.classical_solver: PyTorch LSTM baseline; QLSTM implemented with PyTorch and PennyLane
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: data cleaning, train/test split, standardization, normalization, feature engineering

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: QLSTM loss decreases faster than classical LSTM in both training and testing

speedup_claims.conditions: training and testing on MRK stock forecasting with 4-qubit QLSTM over 20 epochs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports faster convergence qualitatively and via loss curves, but does not provide exact convergence times or statistical significance.
This is a parameter-efficiency comparison, not a runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not analyzed; no asymptotic complexity or scaling study provided.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown. Current experiment uses 4 qubits and a single variational layer on a simulator; no resource estimate for larger datasets or hardware execution.
limiting_factors: Evaluation performed only on a noiseless simulator (PennyLane lightning.qubit).
Very small quantum model (4 qubits, single variational layer).
No quantitative accuracy numbers or statistical tests reported.
Comparison limited to a single classical baseline (LSTM).
No complexity or runtime analysis demonstrating scaling advantage.
Dataset size modest (2,738 trading days) and effectively classical preprocessing dominates.

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly states initial testing was performed on simulators such as lightning.qubit and no real QPU device is named.
Circuit depth not explicitly quantified; only one quantum layer with 3 rotational gates and 4 qubits is reported.
Speedup order is not asymptotically characterized; the paper reports empirical performance improvements only.

The paper claims improved accuracy, faster convergence, and fewer parameters for QLSTM compared to classical LSTM, but provides only qualitative plots and no statistically rigorous or large‑scale demonstration.
Results are obtained on a noiseless simulator rather than quantum hardware.
